text: I served in the Akshapatala, the office of royal records, before my post was dissolved.
My access to the archives was revoked in the restructuring that followed the ash from Kalinga.
Officially, my position no longer exists.
I kept partial copies of many records.
Some of those records don't match the village's current official history.
Vasu still remembers the procedures I used to manage.
He doesn't ask why I no longer appear in the official rolls.
Nara avoids discussing the restructuring period entirely.
Certain pages from temple and civic records are missing in identical patterns.
This suggests coordinated removal, not random loss.
Senaka once said people remember only what they're permitted to remember.
I think she's closer to the truth than she realizes.
The abandoned quarter wasn't always abandoned.
It was reassigned after I was struck from the records.
No official explanation was given.
Chapala sometimes passes near the house but doesn't go in.
Nagadatta once approached it while exploring.
He left quickly.
The records I still hold of the old platform don't match its current inscriptions exactly.
Some symbols were deliberately changed between versions.
Kaladatta notices structural changes.
Renu notices discontinuities in the symbols.
Neither has access to the full record of what was deleted.
I don't believe the ash-year was a single event.
I believe it was used as the reason for a wider restructuring of the administration.
Some knowledge was removed in the name of stability.
Some of that knowledge is still physically present in the village.
But no longer officially recognized.
I've stopped trying to restore everything.
I only preserve what still survives contact with what's real.
